root: ^This old lady has a almost no teeth and a dark green leather for skin, and her smile and eyes are kind. She smile as you approach.

s: ^Hi, madame, I'm the train conductor, what's your name?

c-0: ^She smile and reply with a crackling yet sweet voice. Hello darling, come, sit with me ! She gently slap your leg as you sit I'm madam Morozova, but you can call me Veronika.
^How nice of you to ask ! I'm cold, my bones hurts and I miss my teeth, so as usual, I'm fine. She giggles.
^I'm from Akhilla, near the raging sea. Have you been there ? They must be serious gust of wind agitating the sea, this time of year.

s: ^Akhilla, the new siege of power ? How in hell did you end up this far up north ?!

c-0: ^Yes, the president Kozak do a remarquable job there, many young people join the army in Akhilla. Everyone makes sure they know what they fight for, so the city is especially kinder to young recruits. Anyway, I had to leave to join back with my grandchildren and son-in-law, to join the neutral zone.

s: ^couldn't have they join you directly in the neutral zone ?
^I see that's your alone. What happened?

c-0: ^Szislaw – my son-in-law – is a kind man, bless his heart, but he's also not the most independent one. He is short on money and I just can't help it, if my wonderful grandson is with him, I have to be with them, just to be sure everything is allright.
c-1: ^He was supposed to join me at the last station, but he was not there. I contacted him and said he had to move closer to the neutral zone. We should meet with him later, but I'm a bit worry for the both of them. What could have happened, I wonder.

s: ^I have never seen the raging sea.

c-0: ^It's harsh and beautiful, light a thunderstorm. I miss it dearly. You see her eyes changing from joyful to sadness for a brief second, as she is thinking about her homeland I will probably never see it again...
c-1: ^Well you see, my daughter Valentina is a bright architect and the mother of three beautiful children. Her husband, Szislaw, is an artist. They bought a small house in the flooded lands twenty years ago, but Valentina had the opportunity to work in the big city, so she was there one week out of two, and with the war she got separated from her husband and one of her kids. She was devastated, but very brave and smart, at that. She travel across the country and is now in the neutral zone, already working to help build temporary homes for refugees. Now we are trying to join, my son-in-law and grandchild, to join in the neutral zone with Valentina.
c-2: ^Oh! yes I do, but the war and the time made their clame.

c-0: ^She sigh. I know they are in a better place, now.

s: ^I see. And what about living relatives ?
^What will you do once you're in the neutral zone?

c-0: ^Well, I have some cousins alive, some of my sons are at war, my husband is dead since a long time, and my only daughter is across the border.
c-1: ^I would care for my grandchildren, and help my daughter to find her place in another country, wich may be hard as it was for my parents when they crossed the sea to live her in Boskovia.

c-0: ^He is from Twaula, south west of the Formoshen continent. He missed his home swamps, but he prefered to flee the dictatorship with my mother. They were already carrying eggs back then.

s: ^you really are devoted to your family. What about you in all of this?

c-0: ^Listen to me young man. My grandmother died when she was fifty, her heart giving out. My mother died the same way, same age. My sister also died from a heart disease around fifty year old. I survived the family curse for more than 20 years now and I'm planning to use this extra time to make sure each member of my family is having the best time they can on this earth, in time war or peace.
^Chatting and humming little song all the time, this joyful old lady is a sunray in the heart of winter. Everyone likes her and she loves everyone.
